integration.name: Mailgun
integration.tagline: A sending domain of your own
integration.summary: Send from a domain you have verified in Mailgun. The connection carries both the key and the domain, so it is unambiguous which identity a message leaves as.

credentials.label: API Key
credentials.note: The key for the sending domain. The account-level key also works, but a sending key is the safer one to paste here.

config.label: Sending domain
config.note: Required. Mailgun puts it in the API path, so it must match the verified domain exactly.

config.label: Sender address (From)
config.note: Must be an address on that verified domain.

strengths: The sending domain is part of the connection, so the identity is explicit
Per-domain keys, so the credential can be scoped to one domain
Domain verification stays in your own Mailgun account
considerations: A wrong or unverified domain fails at Mailgun rather than here — the error code is recorded on the send so you can see which check rejected it.
